items.summary: First of all, I'm not claiming that my framework will save industrial C/C++ development. It's just a hobby project. Industrial code needs safer code, not easier code. But when you're developing a blog at 8 PM, long template errors are annoying. You need CRUD and RDBMS. It's simple. CWIST is for that kind of work. It sacrifices memory safety, smart pointers, and modern C++ abstractions. items.title: Show HN: Twain, a diff viewer like Meld, but for the age of AI
items.summary: I love Meld, I've been using it for a while now, it's amazing how many diff viewers exist these days and how they are all awful compared to Meld. But Meld was missing some features that I thought were worth having: - all files from a Git diff shown in the same view, sequentially + a file tree on the side. - show either the full files or only the parts that changed. - tree-sitter-based syntax highlighting. - the ability to comment on sets of changes and lines, and AIs can read these comments. - the ability to search through the entire set of modified files. Twain is in Rust and based on GTK4.
